classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly requested cosine rule to the radius–chord triangle, then interpret road shortening as arc length minus chord length and retain the unrounded angle.

content.prompt: A straight road was constructed to cut a dangerous bend on a country road. It was found that the bend was part of an arc of radius $180$ metres and the straight road was $240$ metres long.

spec.description: Dashed upper circular arc, solid horizontal chord labelled 240 m, and two dashed radii from the centre below, each labelled 180 m with matching single ticks. A central angle mark is labelled θ. Ordinary source blue and grey strokes are rendered black under house style; solid/dashed distinctions remain.
spec.mathematics: Both radii are 180 m and the chord is 240 m. The symmetric coordinate construction has chord-to-radius ratio 4:3 and uses the circular minor arc joining the chord endpoints.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated angle or road-length reduction displayed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the cosine rule to find the size of $\theta$, in radians, correct to two decimal places.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the distance by which the old road was shortened, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded angle from part (a). The old road is the arc and the new road is the chord.

$$\begin{align*}l_{\text{old}}&=r\theta\\l_{\text{old}}&=180\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)\text{ m}\\d_{\text{shortened}}&=l_{\text{old}}-240\\d_{\text{shortened}}&=180\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)-240\\d_{\text{shortened}}&\approx23\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
